<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Appendix C <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Examples</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">C.2</span> Example of a <span class="math inline">\(d\)</span>-dimensional Smooth Manifold (§§<a class="dg-xref" href="../topological-manifolds/charts-topological-manifolds.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Charts_Topological_Manifolds">3.2</a>–<a class="dg-xref" href="../topological-manifolds/smooth-manifolds.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Smooth_Manifolds">3.3</a>)</h1></header>
<p>Consider the 1-dim. (topological) manifold <span class="math inline">\(\left( \mathcal{S}^1, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}^1}, \mathcal{A} \right)_1\)</span> constituted by:</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p>The set <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{S}^1 \coloneqq \left\lbrace q = (q_1, q_2) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : q_1^2 + q_2^2 = 1 \right\rbrace\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>The topology inherited from the standard topology of <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^2\)</span>:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}^1} \coloneqq \left.\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{R}^2}\right\rvert_{\mathcal{S}^1}
            = \left\lbrace \mathcal{S}^1 \cap \mathcal{W} : \mathcal{W} \in \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{R}^2} \right\rbrace.
        \end{align*}</span></p></li>
<li><p>The atlas <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{A}\)</span> formed by four charts, whose domains are open in <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}^1}\)</span> and together cover <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{S}^1\)</span>:  <span class="math display">\[
            \mathcal{A} \coloneqq \left\lbrace
            \begin{array}{c@{\quad} | @{\quad} c}
                \textbf{Upper chart $(\mathcal{U}_\uparrow, \mathscr{X}_\uparrow)$} &amp;
                \textbf{Lower chart $(\mathcal{U}_\downarrow, \mathscr{X}_\downarrow)$} \\[6pt]
                \begin{aligned}
                    \mathcal{U}_\uparrow &amp;\coloneqq \lbrace q \in \mathcal{S}^1 : q_2 &gt; 0 \rbrace \\
                    \mathscr{X}_\uparrow : \mathcal{U}_\uparrow &amp;\longrightarrow \mathscr{X}_\uparrow(\mathcal{U}_\uparrow) = (-1, 1) \\
                    q &amp;\longmapsto \mathscr{X}_\uparrow(q) \coloneqq q_1
                \end{aligned}
                &amp;
                \begin{aligned}
                    \mathcal{U}_\downarrow &amp;\coloneqq \lbrace q \in \mathcal{S}^1 : q_2 &lt; 0 \rbrace \\
                    \mathscr{X}_\downarrow : \mathcal{U}_\downarrow &amp;\longrightarrow \mathscr{X}_\downarrow(\mathcal{U}_\downarrow) = (-1, 1) \\
                    q &amp;\longmapsto \mathscr{X}_\downarrow(q) \coloneqq q_1
                \end{aligned}
                \\[22pt] \hline \\[-2pt]
                \textbf{Right chart $(\mathcal{U}_\rightarrow, \mathscr{X}_\rightarrow)$} &amp;
                \textbf{Left chart $(\mathcal{U}_\leftarrow, \mathscr{X}_\leftarrow)$} \\[6pt]
                \begin{aligned}
                    \mathcal{U}_\rightarrow &amp;\coloneqq \lbrace q \in \mathcal{S}^1 : q_1 &gt; 0 \rbrace \\
                    \mathscr{X}_\rightarrow : \mathcal{U}_\rightarrow &amp;\longrightarrow \mathscr{X}_\rightarrow(\mathcal{U}_\rightarrow) = (-1, 1) \\
                    q &amp;\longmapsto \mathscr{X}_\rightarrow(q) \coloneqq q_2
                \end{aligned}
                &amp;
                \begin{aligned}
                    \mathcal{U}_\leftarrow &amp;\coloneqq \lbrace q \in \mathcal{S}^1 : q_1 &lt; 0 \rbrace \\
                    \mathscr{X}_\leftarrow : \mathcal{U}_\leftarrow &amp;\longrightarrow \mathscr{X}_\leftarrow(\mathcal{U}_\leftarrow) = (-1, 1) \\
                    q &amp;\longmapsto \mathscr{X}_\leftarrow(q) \coloneqq q_2
                \end{aligned}
            \end{array}
            \right\rbrace
        \]</span>  Each chart map is a homeomorphism onto the open interval <span class="math inline">\((-1, 1)\)</span>, with continuous inverse  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathscr{X}_\uparrow^{-1}(\alpha) &amp;= \left( \alpha, \sqrt{1 - \alpha^2} \right), &amp;
            \mathscr{X}_\downarrow^{-1}(\alpha) &amp;= \left( \alpha, -\sqrt{1 - \alpha^2} \right), \\
            \mathscr{X}_\rightarrow^{-1}(\alpha) &amp;= \left( \sqrt{1 - \alpha^2}, \alpha \right), &amp;
            \mathscr{X}_\leftarrow^{-1}(\alpha) &amp;= \left( -\sqrt{1 - \alpha^2}, \alpha \right).
        \end{align*}</span></p></li>
</ol>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p>We now check that the atlas is <span class="math inline">\(C^\infty\)</span>-compatible, i.e. that the chart transition maps are smooth wherever two chart domains overlap. The intersection of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_\uparrow\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_\rightarrow\)</span> is the open quarter of circle <span class="math display">\[
    \mathcal{U}_\uparrow \cap \mathcal{U}_\rightarrow
    = \left\lbrace q \in \mathcal{S}^1 : q_1 &gt; 0, \; q_2 &gt; 0 \right\rbrace,
\]</span></p>
